idiom_name: typed EventTarget wrapper with an event map (or typed EventEmitter)
implementation_notes: TypeScript compiles to the same runtime primitives as JavaScript - EventTarget (browser and Node) or EventEmitter - and adds only the typing that makes a bus safe: declare an event map, constrain publish/subscribe to keyof of that map, and derive the payload type from the event name so publishers and subscribers cannot disagree. The classic channel structure is never written; the type map and the unsubscribe token replace it. RxJS Subject<T> is the typed library alternative when subscribers need operators (filter, throttle, debounce) rather than raw fan-out.
pitfalls: The underlying EventTarget API is string-typed: a typo in an event name compiles and silently never fires unless the wrapper above constrains names to the event map.
Event and EventTarget types differ between DOM and Node libs, so the same file can compile under one tsconfig ("lib"/@types/node combination) and fail under another.
Listeners are retained strongly; not calling the returned unsubscribe token leaks the subscriber for the lifetime of the channel.
